problems.statement: Write $3^{3 x}$ as a single power of $3$.
hints: Use the exponent laws: a power of a power multiplies the exponents.
Keep the base and combine only the exponents.

problems.statement: Write $3^{x} 3^{2 x + 1}$ as a single power of $3$.
hints: Use the exponent laws: when multiplying powers with the same base, add the exponents.
Keep the base and combine only the exponents.
solution: $3^{x} 3^{2 x + 1} = 3^{\frac{\ln{\left(3^{3 x} \right)}}{\ln{\left(3 \right)}} + 1}$ by the exponent laws.
So the single power is $3^{3 x + 1}$.

problems.statement: Write $5^{- x} 5^{3 x + 1}$ as a single power of $5$.
hints: Use the exponent laws: when dividing powers with the same base, subtract the exponents.
Keep the base and combine only the exponents.
solution: $5^{- x} 5^{3 x + 1} = 5^{\frac{\ln{\left(5^{2 x} \right)}}{\ln{\left(5 \right)}} + 1}$ by the exponent laws.
So the single power is $5^{2 x + 1}$.

problems.statement: Write $2 \cdot 2^{2 x}$ as a single power of $2$.
hints: Use the exponent laws: apply the power rule first, then add and subtract exponents.
Keep the base and combine only the exponents.
solution: $2 \cdot 2^{2 x} = 2^{\frac{\ln{\left(2^{2 x} \right)}}{\ln{\left(2 \right)}} + 1}$ by the exponent laws.
So the single power is $2^{2 x + 1}$.

problems.statement: Write $3^{3 x} 3^{2 x + 1}$ as a single power of $3$.
hints: Use the exponent laws: when multiplying powers with the same base, add the exponents.
Keep the base and combine only the exponents.
solution: $3^{3 x} 3^{2 x + 1} = 3^{\frac{\ln{\left(3^{5 x} \right)}}{\ln{\left(3 \right)}} + 1}$ by the exponent laws.
So the single power is $3^{5 x + 1}$.

problems.statement: Write $3^{- x} 3^{2 x + 2}$ as a single power of $3$.
hints: Use the exponent laws: when dividing powers with the same base, subtract the exponents.
Keep the base and combine only the exponents.
solution: $3^{- x} 3^{2 x + 2} = 3^{\frac{\ln{\left(3^{x} \right)}}{\ln{\left(3 \right)}} + 2}$ by the exponent laws.

problems.statement: A culture starts with $500$ cells and triples every $4$ hours. Write the population $P$ as a function of time $t$ in hours.
hints: Each tripling multiplies by $3$; count how many triplings happen in $t$ hours.
After $t$ hours there have been $t/4$ triplings, so the multiplier is $3^{t/4}$.
solution: The population multiplies by $3$ every $4$ hours, giving $3^{t/4}$ after $t$ hours.

problems.statement: Find the range of $f(x) = 3^{x} - 3$. Answer in interval notation.
hints: $3^{x}$ takes every positive value but never $0$ or a negative value.
Multiplying by $1$ keeps it positive; adding $-3$ shifts the whole range.
solution: $3^{x} > 0$ for all $x$ and gets arbitrarily close to $0$ and arbitrarily large.
So $f(x) > -3$ with no upper bound: range $(-3, \infty)$.

problems.statement: Find the range of $f(x) = 3 e^{x} + 1$. Answer in interval notation.
hints: $e^{x}$ takes every positive value but never $0$ or a negative value.
Multiplying by $3$ keeps it positive; adding $1$ shifts the whole range.
solution: $3 e^{x} > 0$ for all $x$ and gets arbitrarily close to $0$ and arbitrarily large.
So $f(x) > 1$ with no upper bound: range $(1, \infty)$.

problems.statement: Find the range of $f(x) = 3 \cdot 2^{x} + 2$. Answer in interval notation.

Multiplying by $3$ keeps it positive; adding $2$ shifts the whole range.
solution: $3 \cdot 2^{x} > 0$ for all $x$ and gets arbitrarily close to $0$ and arbitrarily large.
So $f(x) > 2$ with no upper bound: range $(2, \infty)$.

problems.statement: For very large $x$, which of these functions is eventually the largest?
hints: Compare how each function grows when $x$ is multiplied or increased by a fixed step.
Any exponential function with base greater than 1 eventually outgrows every power of $x$, no matter how large the exponent.
solution: Powers like $x^{50}$ grow by a fixed factor when $x$ is scaled, but $\left(\frac{11}{10}\right)^{x}$ multiplies by $\frac{11}{10}$ for every unit increase in $x$.
Eventually the exponential function exceeds any polynomial, so it is the largest for large $x$.

problems.statement: An account with $5000$ dollars grows by $4\%$ per year, compounded annually. What is the balance after $3$ years? Round to the nearest cent.
hints: Each year multiplies the balance by $1 + r$.
The balance is $5000(1 + \frac{1}{25})^{3}$.
